title: Close a valve by hand after its actuator loses power: declutch, then turn the handwheel
instruction: The valve actuator has lost power. Close the valve by hand: hold the orange lever down and turn the handwheel until the lever stays down by itself, then turn the handwheel clockwise until the indicator's pointer reaches the red CLOSED end.
context: Water, wastewater and process-plant operators close motorised valves by hand during power failures. On electric actuators the handwheel is uncoupled in motor mode and spins without moving the valve; it only drives the valve once the hand/auto lever has been held while the wheel is turned far enough for the clutch to engage. Unlike TK-PW77VZ (turning a gate valve's star handle by regrasping), turning this handwheel does nothing until the other arm has changed the actuator's mode.
setup: Positions are from the robot's view: 'in front' is the distance ahead of the line through the two arm bases, 'right' and 'left' from the midline halfway between them, heights above the table top. Angles round the handwheel's vertical axis are seen from above, 0 degrees pointing straight ahead and 90 degrees to the robot's left. One fixed assembly, centred on the handwheel's axis 30.0 cm in front and 13.0 cm right of the midline. Valve (grey cast iron): a 70 mm cube on the table with a 35 mm pipe stub front and back (120 mm overall, axis 30 mm high). Actuator gearcase (blue-grey painted aluminium): 130 mm front to back, 120 mm wide, 70 to 115 mm high, on the valve. Handwheel (black steel, 0.3 kg), flat on a 20 mm steel shaft on top of the gearcase: a rim of 150 mm centre diameter and 12 x 12 mm section, four 8 mm wide by 12 mm deep spokes starting at 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees, and a 32 mm hub, all centred 135 mm high. Motor housing (blue-grey, fixed to the gearcase): 100 mm front to back, 150 mm wide, 60 mm high, from 6 to 21 cm left of the handwheel axis. Hand/auto lever: an orange 50 x 50 x 8 mm polymer paddle on a stem, centred 2 cm nearer the robot than the wheel axis and 17 cm left of it (4 cm left of the midline), its top 95 mm high; it moves straight down 12 mm against a 1.5 N spring and returns up when released, unless latched. Position indicator, on top of the motor housing 2.5 cm beyond the wheel axis: a white strip 12 mm wide running left 72 mm from 7.5 cm left of the wheel axis, green at its right (OPEN) end and red at its left (CLOSED) end, with a black 16 x 4 x 4 mm pointer that starts at the green end. Behaviour: the handwheel turns freely either way with light drag and the valve does not move (motor mode). If the paddle is held at least 90% down while the wheel passes a clutch dog (50 degrees clockwise from the start, then every 120 degrees either way), the clutch engages and the paddle latches down. From then on, clockwise turning closes the valve: one turn from the engaging position to a closed stop, with an open stop at the engaging position, and the pointer moves from the green end to the red end in proportion. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Engaged: the paddle latched down (it stays down with nothing on it). Closed fraction: the pointer's travel from the green end toward the red end, 60 mm for fully closed (equivalently the wheel's clockwise rotation since engaging, over one turn). Judged at the end of the trial. 1.0: engaged and the valve closed, the wheel within 5 degrees of its closed stop (pointer within 0.4 mm of the red end), held 3 s. 0.5: engaged and at least half closed (pointer at least 30 mm from the green end). 0.25: engaged, less than half closed. 0 otherwise, including any amount of turning the handwheel without the clutch engaged, and any part moved off its fixture or broken.
reset_notes: Unlatch the paddle so it springs up (motor mode), turn the handwheel back to its starting position (spokes at 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees, nearest clutch dog 50 degrees clockwise), and return the pointer to the green end. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Unpowered scale trainer. A real actuator takes tens of handwheel turns to close a valve; here one turn covers the full stroke. The clutch is modelled as engagement events at three dog angles, gated on the paddle being held down, with the paddle latching on engagement (as on lever-latching actuators); the end stops are stiff springs that act only beyond each stop. The indicator pointer is driven in software from the valve's travel. No motor, torque switch, gearbox backlash, flow or automatic return to motor mode is modelled. The layout is fixed, so a memorised replay of the demo cannot be ruled out.
